weak_tools: graph_pathfinding: exact turn scoring and failure boundaries
repeated_mistakes: Treating numeric-looking room names or link endpoints as ints instead of strings.
Passing a full args slice where a single argument string is expected.
Using := and accidentally shadowing an existing variable that should be updated.
Trying to change a range loop index to skip/control future iterations.
Confusing a map lookup value with the key or field being validated.
Writing to a validation map before separating the duplicate check from the accepted insert.
Using negated boolean conditions when the intended check is whether any parser state flag is pending.
solved_concepts: Map lookup by key avoids scanning a slice for known room names.
A command like ##start or ##end marks the next room, not itself.
Main can stay small by delegating parsing to a ParseFile function.
Room parsing can use strings.Fields for name/x/y and strconv.Atoi for integer coordinates.
Pending flags can connect ##start/##end commands to the next parsed room.
Go comma-ok lookup can check whether a map key already exists without needing to inspect struct fields.
A comparable struct like Coord can be used as a map key to track duplicate coordinates.
A comparable Link struct can track duplicate and reversed duplicate tunnels when endpoints are normalized.
Lem-in graph links should be stored as an adjacency list so one room can have multiple neighbors.
Parser line categories can use continue after handling so malformed leftovers are rejected at the bottom of the loop.
Whitespace-only files can be detected by checking trimmed content before splitting into lines.
BFS explores unweighted graph levels and is appropriate for shortest Lem-in paths.
A predecessor map from room to previous room is enough to reconstruct a discovered path.
Following predecessors from end to start builds a reversed path, which can be reversed into start-to-end order.
A function that returns a path and an error should detect its local error, while main handles the returned error and output.
A turn of Lem-in moves is a slice of strings, while all turns form a nested slice.
For turn scheduling, rebuild next active state instead of removing elements while ranging over the current active slice.
A path's final valid room index is its length minus one.
A multi-path coordinator can repeatedly call a single-path BFS while preserving blocked state outside the helper.
For undirected tunnels, normalize endpoint order before using a combined string as a map key.

For multi-path ant assignment, reset a first-path candidate each turn and choose the minimum of path length plus that path's assigned-ant count; a strict comparison preserves the first candidate on ties.
When a turn needs multiple launches, process existing ants first, record intermediate occupied rooms for that turn, then launch new ants directly into next-turn active state.
A repeated launch loop must re-run available-path selection after each launch and stop when no first intermediate room is available.
strings.Join can format a slice of move strings with separators while avoiding a trailing separator.
A later path-search failure can be normal completion when at least one valid path was already found.
The parser's adjacency map records each undirected tunnel in both directions; normalized endpoints are only needed for duplicate tracking.
A direct start-to-end route does not occupy the end room or remain active, but its tunnel may be used only once per turn.
The solver first advances active ants, then launches new ants into currently available first rooms.
Greedily keeping the first shortest BFS path can prevent a larger, faster set of mutually compatible paths; DFS with backtracking is a candidate-path discovery approach.
DFS keeps visited state local to its current branch: it marks and appends a neighbor before recursion, then removes and unmarks it during backtracking.
A completed DFS path must be copied before it is stored, because later backtracking changes the current path slice.
Go source files in one directory with the same package declaration share unexported functions and must not import that package itself.
A tunnel key can be normalized from its two endpoint room names so either travel direction maps to the same per-turn occupancy entry.
A struct can keep selected paths, their assigned-ant counts, and their score coherent across package boundaries when its type and needed fields are exported.
A solver must receive and obey the same per-path allocation that was used to score a path selection; otherwise its independent launch choices can lose the optimal makespan.
A stable sort preserves DFS order for paths of equal length while allowing a deterministic short-path-first selector traversal.
Standard deviation represents data spread in the same units as the original values and can guide a statistical prediction interval.
Mean requires only sum divided by count; standard deviation additionally squares distances from that mean, averages them, and takes the square root.
Prediction-range quality is evaluated by a trade-off: correct coverage earns points, but wider intervals earn fewer points, so Final Result is more meaningful than accuracy percentage alone.
A per-path slice of ant IDs records assignment, while a separate per-path index identifies the next assigned ant to launch.
A recursive include branch returns after all deeper combinations are explored; only then does slice/map backtracking undo the current choice before the unconditional exclude branch runs.
